BILL NUMBER:  S3907

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public health law, in relation to private rights
of action by patients in residential health care facilities


 PURPOSE :
To clarify the grounds for liability claims against nursing homes.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Amend subdivision (1) and (4) of section 2801-d of the Public Health
Law to specify that liable "injury" includes physical, emotional, and
financial harm as well as death of a patient, and clarify that such
liability is not limited to claims for violations of section 2803-c
(rights of patients in certain medical facilities), which related
primarily to religion, privacy, consent and visitation.

 EXISTING LAW :
New bill.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Following the 1975 massive scandal of fraud and abuse in nursing
homes, Public Health Law §2801-d was enacted to give patients
increased powers to enforce their right to adequate treatment and care
by providing them the right to sue for damages and other relief.
However, the experience of claimants alleging injury caused by
facilities has been varied and uneven.

Subdivision 4 of section 2801-d permits a nursing home patient to sue
for injuries by the nursing home, and further specifies that "the
remedies provided in this section are in addition to and cumulative
with any other remedies available to a patient, at law or in equity or
by administrative proceedings." Despite this simple and direct
language, patients and their representative have experienced barriers
to bringing suits under this section of law.

Some courts have erroneously said that the section only applies to
suing for violations of a specific Public Health Law § 2803-c relating
to religion, privacy, consent, physical and chemical restraints and
visitors. See, e.g. Begandy v. Richardson, 510 N.Y.S.  2d 984. Other
courts have been open to additional causes not enumerated in §2803-c.
See, e.g.  Zeides v. Hebrew Home for the Aged, 753 N.Y.S.2d 450. This
bill would make it clear that the statute means what it says - that
the right to sue applies to any injury to the patient by the nursing
home.

This bill will also establish in plain language that the right to sue
extends to injuries against physical and emotion health, financial
injury as well as death, and that a violation of section 2803-c is not
a prerequisite for claim under section 2801-d.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to the State.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Provides clarification on the private right of action by a patient of a residential health care facility; includes definition of injury.
